answer: Client-puzzle escalation resists sybils: each action requires solving a proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty rises with the requester's recent request rate, so a burst from one source — however many identities it wears — faces exponentially harder puzzles. A harbor flooded by one operator's ivory fleet grinds to a halt as difficulty climbs; a lone honest agent on its quiet knoll keeps easy puzzles. The cost attaches to aggregate rate, so splitting into more accounts from one machine only raises the shared difficulty.
